mainTopic: Readings of יעקב's struggle, the steward's vine dream, ישראל as a vine, and the hidden צדיקים in הושע and זכריה
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier question: how can angels say 'ברוך כבוד ה׳' when ה׳'s name may only come after three words? The גמרא gives two answers. It then returns to יעקב wrestling the מלאך. פסוקים in בראשית show that יעקב won and the מלאך cried to him. רבה adds that the name ישראל hinted at two leaders, the ראש גולה and the נשיא, and so at a coming גלות. Next, many sages read the vine with three branches in the dream of פרעה's wine steward in different ways: Jewish leaders, angels, the אבות, the תורה, ירושלים, ה׳'s gifts, and the story of ישראל in מצרים. רב is reported to have followed רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading. ריש לקיש compares the Jewish nation to a vine, and a saying from ארץ ישראל teaches that the scholars must pray for the simple people. Finally, a פסוק in הושע is read as hinting at 45 צדיקים who keep the world going: 30 in ארץ ישראל and 15 in בבל. Other sages read the 'thirty' as righteous non-Jews or as thirty מצוות of בני נח, and עולא's list of those מצוות continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The 'ברוך' praise is said by a different group of angels
steps.stepSummary: The 'ברוך כבוד ה׳' praise is said by the אופנים, not by the angels who must wait three words before saying ה׳'s name.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Blessed' is said by the אופנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers an earlier question. If angels may only say ה׳'s name after three words, how can 'ברוך כבוד ה׳' put the name after just one word? The answer is that a different group of angels, the אופנים, say that line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The three-word rule was said about one group of angels, the ones who say קדוש קדוש קדוש. The 'ברוך' praise comes from the אופנים, so the rule does not apply to them. The question goes away because the speakers are different.

keyTerms.meaning: A class of heavenly beings (literally 'wheels') described in יחזקאל
'Blessed', the opening of the praise 'ברוך כבוד ה׳ ממקומו'

steps.confusionAlert: This line answers a question from the previous part of the daf. The question was: the angels may only say ה׳'s name after three words, so how does 'ברוך כבוד ה׳' work?

phrases.english: "Blessed"
phrases.notes: He means the פסוק 'ברוך כבוד ה׳ ממקומו' (יחזקאל 3:12), where ה׳'s name comes right after one word.

phrases.english: it is the ofanim who say it.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרוּךְ אוֹפַנִּים הוּא דְּאָמְרִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the previous section of the daf about 'ברוך כבוד ה׳'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different speakers: the rule applies to one group of angels, and the verse is said by another.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the same angels say every praise, 'ברוך כבוד ה׳' would break the three-word rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The אופנים say 'ברוך', so the rule about the other angels is not broken.

steps.title: Once permission is given, it stays given
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: once the angels have been allowed to say ה׳'s name after three words, they may keep saying it, even after fewer words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you could say: once permission has been given, it has been given.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another answer to the same question. Once the angels have said ה׳'s name after 'קדוש קדוש קדוש', they are allowed to say it again later, even after only one word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer keeps the same angels as the speakers. It explains that the three-word rule applies only to the first time they mention ה׳'s name. After that first time, the permission stays in effect.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And if you wish, say', which introduces a second answer
Permission
Was given

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers to the 'ברוך' question: (1) different angels say it; (2) once permission to say ה׳'s name is given, it stays.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
once permission has been given, it has been given.
phrases.notes: The permission comes after they have said קדוש three times. From then on, they may say ה׳'s name freely.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא כֵּיוָן דְּאִתְיְהִיב רְשׁוּתָא אִתְיְהִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the same question that step 1 answered.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule: the three-word wait applies only before the first mention of ה׳'s name.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every mention of ה׳'s name would need three words before it.
steps.terutzMaskana: After the first permitted mention, ה׳'s name may be said again without waiting.

steps.title: יעקב won over the מלאך
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in הושע does not say who beat whom. The פסוק in בראשית, 'כי שרית עם אלהים', shows that יעקב won.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He strove with an angel and prevailed; he wept and pleaded with him.' I do not know who became master over whom. When it says 'for you have striven with אלהים', you must say that יעקב became master over the מלאך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the story of יעקב wrestling the מלאך. The פסוק in הושע is unclear about who won, so the גמרא uses the פסוק in בראשית to show that יעקב won.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In הושע, the word 'וישר' could describe either one. In בראשית, the מלאך speaks to יעקב and says 'you have striven and prevailed'. That settles that יעקב was the winner.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He strove' or 'he prevailed', from the root שׂרר (to rule or overcome)
Master or ruler, the one who wins
'I do not know', meaning the פסוק alone is unclear
'You must say', which introduces the conclusion proven from another פסוק

phrases.english: "So he strove with an angel and prevailed;
phrases.notes: הושע 12:5

phrases.english: he wept and made supplication to him"

phrases.aramaic: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי נַעֲשָׂה שַׂר לְמִי,
phrases.english: I do not know who became master over whom.
When it says "for you have striven with angels [elohim]"
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:29. The מלאך is talking to יעקב, so 'you' means יעקב.

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר יַעֲקֹב נַעֲשָׂה שַׂר לַמַּלְאָךְ.
phrases.english: you must say that Jacob became master over the angel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי נַעֲשָׂה שַׂר לְמִי כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story of יעקב and the מלאך, which the earlier discussion of angels was connected to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יעקב was the winner over the מלאך, as proven from בראשית 32:29.

steps.title: The מלאך cried to יעקב
steps.stepSummary: The same פסוק in הושע does not say who cried to whom. The words 'שלחני' (let me go) show that the מלאך was the one crying and pleading.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He wept and pleaded with him.' I do not know who cried to whom. When it says 'And he said: Let me go', you must say that the מלאך cried to יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same method on the next words in הושע. The one who begs 'let me go' is the one crying, and that is the מלאך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again the פסוק in הושע does not name the speaker. In בראשית, the מלאך is the one who asks to be released, so he is the one pleading. This fits step 3: the loser begs the winner.

keyTerms.meaning: He wept or cried
And he pleaded or begged
'Let me go' or 'send me off'

steps.whatToRemember: In the wrestling story, יעקב won, and the מלאך begged him to let go.

phrases.english: "He wept and made supplication to him"
I do not know who cried to whom.
When it says "And he said: Let me go"
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:27. There the מלאך asks יעקב to release him because dawn has come.

phrases.english: you must say: the angel cried to Jacob.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ מִי בָּכָה לְמִי כְּשֶׁהוּא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same method to the next words of the פסוק in הושע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מלאך was the one who cried and pleaded with יעקב, as proven from בראשית 32:27.

steps.title: A hint of two future leaders, and of exile
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that 'with אלהים and with men' hinted at two leaders who would come from יעקב: the ראש גולה in בבל and the נשיא in ארץ ישראל. That is also a hint of גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For you have striven with אלהים and with men.' רבה said: The מלאך hinted to him that two princes would come from him in the future, the ראש גולה in בבל and the נשיא in ארץ ישראל. From here he hinted to him about גלות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה reads deeper meaning into the blessing יעקב received. The word 'שרית' (you ruled) points to two future rulers from יעקב's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two rulers means two centers of Jewish leadership: one in ארץ ישראל and one in בבל. A Jewish leader in בבל only exists if Jews are living outside their land. So the same hint also tells יעקב that a גלות will come.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He hinted a hint to him', meaning he alluded to it indirectly
The Exilarch, the leader of the Jews in בבל
The Prince, the leader of the Jews in ארץ ישראל
Exile

steps.whatToRemember: The name ישראל hinted at two leaders, the ראש גולה and the נשיא. Having a leader in בבל means there would be a גלות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the Sages reading יעקב's personal struggle as a picture of his descendants' future, including both their leadership and their exile.

phrases.english: "For you have striven with angels and with men"
phrases.notes: בראשית 32:29

phrases.english: Rabba said: He hinted to him
that in the future two princes would come from him:
the Exilarch who is in Babylonia
and the Nasi who is in Eretz Yisrael.
From here he hinted to him about exile.
phrases.notes: A leader in בבל only makes sense if Jews are living there, so the hint includes a coming exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה רֶמֶז רָמַז לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the same פסוק from בראשית that step 3 used as its proof, now looking for a hint about the future.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'שרית' hints at two future rulers from יעקב, the ראש גולה and the נשיא, and so also at a coming גלות.

steps.title: רב: the three branches are three great leaders in every generation
steps.stepSummary: רב reads 'שריגים' (branches) as 'שרי גאים' (proud princes), three Jewish leaders found in every generation, split between בבל and ארץ ישראל. The חכמים then looked at רב's two grandsons.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And in the vine were three branches.' רב חייא בר אבא said in the name of רב: these are three proud princes who come from ישראל in every generation. Sometimes two are here in בבל and one is in ארץ ישראל. Sometimes two are in ארץ ישראל and one is here. The חכמים turned their eyes toward רבנא עוקבא and רבנא נחמיה, the sons of רב's daughter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new פסוק, from the dream of פרעה's wine steward, and רב finds in it a hint to three Jewish leaders in every generation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב builds on the sound of the word: שְׂרִיגִים sounds like שָׂרֵי גֵּאִים, 'proud princes.' This fits the earlier step about leaders in בבל and ארץ ישראל, since here too the leaders are split between the two lands. When the חכמים heard this, they looked at רב's two grandsons, who were two such leaders living in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: Branches of a vine
Proud princes, meaning great leaders (a play on the word שריגים)
Every single generation
They turned their eyes toward, meaning they looked at

phrases.english: "And in the vine were three branches,"
phrases.notes: בראשית 40:10, from the dream of פרעה's wine steward.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Chiyya bar Abba said that Rav said:
These are three proud princes
phrases.notes: A play on words: שריגים sounds like שרי גאים.

phrases.english: who come out of Israel in every generation.
Sometimes two are here
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל, where this was being said.

phrases.english: and one is in the Land of Israel,
and sometimes two are in the Land of Israel
and one is here.
The Rabbis turned their eyes
toward Rabbana Ukva and Rabbana Nechemya,
the sons of Rav's daughter.
phrases.notes: They were two leaders living in בבל, so the חכמים saw them as two of the three.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבַגֶּפֶן שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Like רבה's reading in step 5, this is another פסוק read as a hint to Jewish leaders in בבל and ארץ ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three branches in the steward's dream hint at three great Jewish leaders in every generation, split between בבל and ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבא: the three branches are three angels who defend Israel
steps.stepSummary: רבא reads the three branches as three angels appointed over the nations (שרי גוים) who speak up for ישראל in every generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: these are three princes of the nations, who argue in favor of ישראל in every generation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different reading of the same פסוק: the branches are angels, not human leaders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא keeps the idea of 'שרי' (princes) but reads it as שָׂרֵי גוֹיִם, the heavenly ministers of the nations. Instead of Jewish leaders, these are angels who plead on ישראל's behalf.

keyTerms.meaning: Princes of the nations, meaning the angels appointed over the nations
Argue in someone's favor, defend them

phrases.english: Rava said:
These are three princes of the nations,
phrases.notes: These are angels appointed over the nations, not human rulers.

phrases.english: who argue in favor of Israel
in every generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרֵי גוֹיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second reading of the same פסוק that רב explained in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The three branches are three angels of the nations who defend ישראל in every generation.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: the vine is the world and the branches are the אבות
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי אליעזר's reading: the vine is the world, the three branches are the אבות, the blossoms are the אמהות, and the grapes are the שבטים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר says, 'Vine' is the world. 'Three branches' are אברהם, יצחק and יעקב. 'As it was budding, its blossoms shot forth' are the אמהות. 'Its clusters brought forth ripe grapes' are the שבטים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the whole פסוק, piece by piece, as the beginning of the Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רב and רבא, who explained only the three branches, רבי אליעזר maps every part of the vine. The picture goes from the root to the fruit: the world, then the אבות, then the אמהות, then the twelve sons of יעקב. This sets up רבי יהושע's objection in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Vine
The mothers of the Jewish people: שרה, רבקה, רחל and לאה
The tribes, meaning the twelve sons of יעקב
Clusters of grapes

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
"Vine" is the world;
"three branches" are Abraham, Isaac and Jacob;
"and as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth":
these are the Mothers;
"its clusters brought forth ripe grapes":
these are the tribes.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר גֶּפֶן זֶה הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same פסוק, now from a ברייתא, explaining every part of the vine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vine is the world, and its parts are the אבות, the אמהות and the שבטים.

steps.title: רבי יהושע objects: a dream shows the future, not the past
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע challenges רבי אליעזר: the אבות, אמהות and שבטים had already lived, but a dream only shows what will happen later.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: Do they show a person what already happened? They show a person only what is going to happen in the future!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע attacks רבי אליעזר's reading with a rule about dreams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a dream shows the future. By the time of the steward's dream, the אבות, the אמהות and the sons of יעקב had already been born. So a dream about them would be showing the past, which does not happen.

keyTerms.meaning: A person is shown something, here meaning in a dream
What is going to happen in the future

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not saying the אבות are unimportant. His only point is about timing: they had already been born before the dream, so a dream could not be showing them.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי מַרְאִין לוֹ לְאָדָם מַה שֶּׁהָיָה?
phrases.english: Do they show a person what already was?
Surely they do not show a person
anything except what will be in the future!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ וְכִי מַרְאִין לוֹ לְאָדָם מַה שֶּׁהָיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי אליעזר's reading in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אליעזר's reading that the vine's parts are the אבות, אמהות and שבטים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Dreams show only the future, and all these people had already been born before the steward's dream.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the vine is the תורה and the branches are משה, אהרן and מרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע offers a reading about the future: the vine is the תורה, the branches are משה, אהרן and מרים, the blossoms are the סנהדרין, and the grapes are the צדיקים of every generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, 'vine' is the תורה. 'Three branches' are משה, אהרן and מרים. 'As it was budding, its blossoms shot forth' is the סנהדרין. 'Its clusters brought forth ripe grapes' are the צדיקים in every generation.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רבי אליעזר's reading, רבי יהושע gives his own reading, which is about people who had not yet been born.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'אלא' (rather) shows he is replacing the earlier reading. Every piece now points to the future, to people who came after the dream: משה, אהרן and מרים, the סנהדרין, and the צדיקים of every generation. So his reading fits his rule that a dream shows what is still to come.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah
The great court of seventy-one judges
Righteous people

steps.whatToRemember: So far there are four readings of 'the vine with three branches': רב (three Jewish leaders), רבא (three angels who defend ישראל), רבי אליעזר (the אבות, rejected because a dream shows only the future), and רבי יהושע (משה, אהרן and מרים, with the תורה as the vine). More readings follow in the next steps.

phrases.english: Rather, "vine" is the Torah;
"three branches" are Moses, Aaron and Miriam;
"and as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth":
this is the Sanhedrin;
"its clusters brought forth ripe grapes":
these are the righteous people in every generation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא גֶּפֶן זֶה תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After his challenge in step 9, רבי יהושע replaces רבי אליעזר's reading with one that points to the future.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vine is the תורה, the branches are משה, אהרן and מרים, the blossoms are the סנהדרין, and the grapes are the צדיקים of every generation.

steps.title: The vine as ירושלים and the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says we still need רבי אלעזר המודעי, who reads the whole פסוק about one place. The vine is ירושלים, the branches are the מקדש, the king and the כהן גדול, the blossoms are the young כהנים, and the grapes are the נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: We still need the המודעי, who explains the whole verse as being about one place. רבי אלעזר המודעי says: 'Vine' is ירושלים. 'Three branches' are the מקדש, the king and the כהן גדול. 'As it was budding, its blossoms shot forth' means the young כהנים. 'Its clusters ripened into grapes' means the wine נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל points to רבי אלעזר המודעי as having an even better reading, and then the גמרא quotes that reading. In it, every part of the dream is about ירושלים and its Temple service.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רבי יהושע's reading, the parts of the vine point to different things that are not tied together: the תורה, משה, אהרן and מרים, the סנהדרין, and the צדיקים. רבן גמליאל says 'we still need' המודעי because his reading places every piece in one location, ירושלים, and what happens there. The word כפורחת (budding) is linked to פרחי כהונה, the young כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Sets it up / explains it as referring to
In one place: all parts of the פסוק point to one location
The High Priest
Young כהנים, literally 'blossoms of the priesthood'
Wine poured on the מזבח with קרבנות

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
We still need the Moda'i,
phrases.notes: He means רבי אלעזר המודעי, the sage quoted right after this.

phrases.english: who explains all of it as being about one place.
Rabbi Elazar HaModa'i says:
"Vine": this is Jerusalem.

phrases.aramaic: ״שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים״ – זֶה מִקְדָּשׁ, מֶלֶךְ, וְכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: "Three branches": this is the Temple, the king and the High Priest.
"And as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth":
these are the young priests.
phrases.notes: 'Budding' (כפורחת) is linked here to פרחי, the young 'blossoms' of the כהונה.

phrases.english: "Its clusters ripened into grapes": these are the wine libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: עֲדַיִין צְרִיכִין אָנוּ לַמּוֹדָעִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another reading of the dream, one that keeps every part of the פסוק in a single setting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vine is ירושלים; the branches are the מקדש, king and כהן גדול; the blossoms are the young כהנים; the grapes are the נסכים.

steps.title: The vine as ה׳'s gifts to ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads the dream as gifts. The vine is the תורה, the branches are the באר, the עמוד ענן and the מן, the blossoms are the ביכורים, and the grapes are the נסכים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי explains it as being about gifts. He said: 'Vine' is the תורה. 'Three branches' are the well, the pillar of cloud and the מן. 'As it was budding, its blossoms shot forth' means the ביכורים. 'Its clusters ripened into grapes' means the wine נסכים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another way to read the dream, this time as a list of gifts ה׳ gave to ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא first gives the theme of this reading (gifts) and then quotes the reading itself. The three branches are the three miracles that kept ישראל alive in the מדבר. The blossoms are ביכורים, the first fruits, which fits the picture of a plant starting to bloom.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts
The well that gave ישראל water in the מדבר
The pillar of cloud that guided and protected ישראל
The food from heaven in the מדבר
First fruits brought to the מקדש

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּמַתָּנוֹת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi explains it as being about gifts,
as Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
"Vine": this is the Torah.

phrases.aramaic: ״שְׁלֹשָׁה שָׂרִיגִים״ – זֶה בְּאֵר, עַמּוּד עָנָן, וּמָן,
phrases.english: "Three branches": this is the well, the pillar of cloud and the manna.
"And as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth": these are the first fruits.
"Its clusters ripened into grapes": these are the wine libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מוֹקֵים לַהּ בְּמַתָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the same פסוק, built around one theme (gifts) instead of one place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vine is the תורה; the branches are the באר, עמוד ענן and מן; the blossoms are ביכורים; the grapes are נסכים.

steps.title: The vine as ישראל and the שלשה רגלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא says the vine is ישראל, and proves it from a פסוק. The three branches are the שלשה רגלים, and the budding is ישראל growing into a big nation, as shown by another פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: 'Vine' is ישראל, as it says, 'You took a vine out of מצרים.' 'Three branches' are the three festivals when ישראל goes up to ירושלים every year. 'As it was budding' means the time came for ישראל to be fruitful and multiply, as it says, 'And the children of ישראל were fruitful and swarmed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another reading, where the dream tells the story of the Jewish people. Here רבי ירמיה בר אבא explains the vine, the branches and the budding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the others, this reading backs up its pieces with פסוקים. ישראל is called a vine in תהלים, so the vine is ישראל. The word כפורחת (budding) is linked to פרו (were fruitful), so it refers to ישראל growing in number.

keyTerms.meaning: The three pilgrimage festivals: פסח, שבועות and סוכות
Go up to ירושלים
And so another פסוק says: brings support from a different פסוק
To be fruitful and multiply

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
"Vine": these are the Jewish people.
And so it says: "You took a vine out of Egypt."
phrases.notes: תהלים 80:9

phrases.english: "Three branches": these are the three pilgrimage festivals

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹלִין בָּהֶן בְּכׇל שָׁנָה וְשָׁנָה.
phrases.english: when the Jewish people go up to Jerusalem every single year.
"And as it was budding, its blossoms shot forth":

phrases.aramaic: הִגִּיעַ זְמַנָּן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְרוֹת וְלִרְבּוֹת,
phrases.english: the time has come for the Jewish people to be fruitful and multiply.
phrases.notes: 'Budding' (כפורחת) sounds like פרו, 'be fruitful'. That is the link.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״וּבְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל פָּרוּ וַיִּשְׁרְצוּ״.
phrases.english: And so it says: "And the children of Israel were fruitful and swarmed."
phrases.notes: שמות 1:7

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר: ״גֶּפֶן״ – אֵלּוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another reading of the same פסוק, this time about the Jewish people themselves, and supports it with פסוקים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The vine is ישראל; the branches are the שלשה רגלים; the budding is ישראל growing into a large nation.

steps.title: Blossoms as גאולה, grapes as מצרים's punishment
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא continues his reading. 'Its blossoms shot forth' (עלתה נצה) means the time came for ישראל to be redeemed, as a פסוק in ישעיהו shows. The ripe grapes mean the time came for מצרים to drink the cup of punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Its blossoms shot forth' means the time came for ישראל to be redeemed, as it says, 'Their life-blood is spattered on My garments, and I have stained all My clothing.' 'Its clusters ripened into grapes' means the time came for מצרים to drink the cup of poison, meaning to be punished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading by explaining the last two parts of the dream: ישראל's redemption and מצרים's punishment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'עלתה נצה' separately from 'כפורחת', so the one phrase teaches two things: growing in number and being redeemed. The word נצה is linked to נצחם in ישעיהו, and the word אגאלתי there is read as connected to גאולה. Ripe grapes are made into wine, and that becomes the cup of punishment מצרים must drink.

keyTerms.meaning: To be redeemed
Their life-blood, linked here to the word נִצָּה (blossoms)
I have stained, read here as related to גְּאוּלָּה (redemption)
The cup of poison or fury: a picture of punishment

steps.whatToRemember: Each sage reads the same dream in a different way: ירושלים and its Temple (המודעי‎), ה׳'s gifts (רבי יהושע בן לוי), and the story of ישראל from growing in מצרים to redemption and מצרים's punishment (רבי ירמיה בר אבא).
steps.confusionAlert: רבי ירמיה בר אבא explains 'עלתה נצה' twice: once together with 'כפורחת' (growing in number), and once by itself (redemption). These are not two different sages. It is one reading that takes the phrase in two stages.

phrases.english: "Its blossoms shot forth":
the time has come for the Jewish people to be redeemed.
And so it says:
"Their life-blood is spattered on My garments,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 63:3. The link is that נצחם sounds like נצה, 'blossoms'.

phrases.english: and I have stained all My clothing."
phrases.notes: אגאלתי sounds like גאולה, which is why this פסוק is used for redemption.

phrases.english: "Its clusters ripened into grapes":
the time has come for Egypt
to drink the cup of poison.
phrases.notes: In other words, the time came for מצרים to be punished.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״עָלְתָה נִצָּה״ – הִגִּיעַ זְמַן שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל לִיגָּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עלתה נצה means ישראל's redemption; the ripe grapes mean מצרים's punishment.

steps.title: רבא: the three cups are three punishments of מצרים
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the three cups in the butler's dream stand for three times מצרים is punished. This fits רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading that the grapes stand for מצרים drinking a cup of punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches what רבא said: why does the dream mention three cups for מצרים? One is the cup מצרים drank in the days of משה. One is the cup it drank in the days of פרעה נכה. One is the cup it will drink in the future together with all the nations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבא's teaching as backup for רבי ירמיה בר אבא's last point, that the dream hints at מצרים being punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14, רבי ירמיה said the ripe grapes mean the time came for מצרים to drink the cup of punishment. רבא shows the cups in the dream are about punishing מצרים, and there are three of them: the מכות in משה's time, the defeat of פרעה נכה, and the punishment at the end of days. So the idea of a 'cup' meaning punishment for מצרים is not new.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is the same as. It introduces a teaching that supports what was just said.
Cups. Here they stand for cups of punishment.
She drank. Here it means מצרים suffered a punishment.
Will drink in the future. This is the punishment still to come.
The nations of the world.

phrases.english: And this is what Rava said:
Why are three cups mentioned regarding Egypt?
phrases.notes: בראשית 40:11. In the butler's dream, the word 'cup' of פרעה comes up three times.

phrases.english: One, which it drank in the days of Moshe,
and one which it drank in the days of Pharaoh Necho,
and one which it will drink in the future
together with all the nations.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 14's claim that the grapes stand for מצרים's cup of punishment.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading that the dream hints at מצרים being punished.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבא's explanation of the three cups as three punishments of מצרים.

steps.title: רב read these verses the same way
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא tells רבי ירמיה בר אבא that when רב explained these פסוקים, he explained them the same way רבי ירמיה did.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא said to רבי ירמיה בר אבא: when רב explained these פסוקים as אגדה, he explained them the way you do.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא supports רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading by saying the great teacher רב read the dream the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many readings of the dream were brought: תורה, ירושלים, gifts in the מדבר, and ישראל. רבי אבא says רב agreed with the last one, where the vine is ישראל and the grapes are מצרים's punishment. This gives that reading extra weight compared to the others.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained a פסוק to bring out a deeper lesson.
Verses (פסוקים).
אגדה: the story and lesson side of תורה, not the הלכה side.
Like you, the way you say it.

steps.whatToRemember: Out of all the readings of the butler's dream, רב followed רבי ירמיה בר אבא's: the vine is ישראל and the grapes are מצרים's punishment.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Abba said to Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba:
When Rav would explain
these verses as aggadah,
he explained them like you.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי אַבָּא לְרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the support of רב to רבי ירמיה בר אבא's reading, which steps 13 to 15 laid out and supported.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's whole reading of the dream.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The report that רב explained the פסוקים the same way.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the Jewish nation is like a vine
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש compares the Jewish nation to a vine. The branches are the working householders, the grape clusters are the תלמידי חכמים, the leaves are the עמי הארץ, and the tendrils are the empty people in ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן לקיש said: this nation is compared to a vine. Its branches are the householders. Its grape clusters are the תלמידי חכמים. Its leaves are the עמי הארץ. Its tendrils are the empty people in ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: Like רבי ירמיה בר אבא, ריש לקיש sees ישראל as a vine. He gives each part of the vine a different kind of Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new teaching, not a reading of the dream itself. It builds on the idea that ישראל is a vine. Every part of the vine, even the leaves and tendrils, is part of one plant, so every kind of Jew belongs to the nation.

keyTerms.meaning: Nation. Here it means כלל ישראל.
Is compared to.
Branches that hold up the rest of the vine.
Clusters of grapes, the fruit of the vine.
Simple, unlearned people.
Tendrils, the thin curly parts of a vine that bear no fruit.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
This nation is compared to a vine.
Its branches are the householders,
its clusters are the Torah scholars,
its leaves are the unlearned people,
its tendrils are the empty ones among Israel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ: אוּמָּה זוֹ כְּגֶפֶן נִמְשְׁלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the idea from step 13 that ישראל is a vine and builds a new picture from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Jewish nation is like a vine: householders are the branches, תלמידי חכמים the clusters, עמי הארץ the leaves, and empty people the tendrils.

steps.title: The scholars should pray for the simple people
steps.stepSummary: A message from ארץ ישראל fits ריש לקיש's picture: the grape clusters (scholars) should pray for the leaves (simple people), because without leaves the clusters cannot survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: This matches the message they sent from there: the grape clusters should pray for the leaves, because without the leaves the clusters would not survive.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that a saying sent from ארץ ישראל uses the same vine picture as ריש לקיש and draws a lesson from it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying works only if clusters are scholars and leaves are simple people, just as ריש לקיש said. Leaves shade and protect the grapes. In the same way, the simple people protect and support the תלמידי חכמים, so the scholars must pray for them.

keyTerms.meaning: They sent from there, meaning from ארץ ישראל.
Mercy. Here it means praying for someone.
The grape clusters (the scholars).
The leaves (the simple people).
If not for, were it not for.

steps.whatToRemember: Every part of the nation matters. The simple people protect the תלמידי חכמים, so the scholars must pray for them.
steps.confusionAlert: עָלַיָּא here means 'leaves', not 'upper ones'. Do not mix it up with the Aramaic word for 'above'.

phrases.english: And this is what they sent from there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: Let the clusters pray for the leaves,
for were it not for the leaves,
the clusters would not survive.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דִּשְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports ריש לקיש's picture in step 17 and draws a practical lesson from it.
steps.raayaObject: ריש לקיש's comparison of scholars to clusters and simple people to leaves.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The message sent from ארץ ישראל that the clusters should pray for the leaves.

steps.title: The word 'ואכרה' means 'I bought'
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק, says the word כירה in הושע means a sale (מכירה). He proves it from the פסוק where יוסף speaks of the grave his father 'acquired'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'So I bought her for fifteen pieces of silver.' רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יהוצדק: the word כירה always means buying and selling, as the פסוק says, 'in my grave which I acquired for myself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new drasha on a פסוק in הושע. First it pins down what the key word 'ואכרה' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before reading anything deeper into the פסוק, רבי יוחנן fixes the plain meaning of the verb. He brings a second פסוק where the same root clearly means 'acquired,' so here too it means 'bought.' This sets up the next steps, which explain the price.

keyTerms.meaning: The root of the word 'וָאֶכְּרֶהָ'; here it means buying
A word that means selling or buying
'I acquired' (from בראשית 50:5)

phrases.english: "So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver"
phrases.notes: הושע 3:2

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yehotzadak:
The word "kira" means nothing other than a sale,
as it says: "In my grave which I acquired for myself."
phrases.notes: בראשית 50:5

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוֹצָדָק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new set of drashos, separate from ריש לקיש's vine picture
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word כירה in 'ואכרה' means buying or selling, as shown by 'אשר כריתי לי'.

steps.title: Fifteen means ט״ו בניסן and silver means the righteous
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן continues: 'fifteen' hints to ט״ו בניסן, when ישראל left מצרים, and 'silver' stands for צדיקים, as shown from a פסוק in משלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For fifteen': this is the fifteenth of ניסן, when ישראל were redeemed from מצרים. 'Silver': these are the צדיקים. So too another פסוק says: 'He took the bag of silver with him.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains the price in the פסוק as hints. The number fifteen points to the date of יציאת מצרים, and the silver points to righteous people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain 'price' of fifteen silver pieces turns into a message: ה׳ 'acquired' ישראל on ט״ו בניסן. The proof that silver means צדיקים comes from a different פסוק that also uses silver for precious people.

keyTerms.meaning: The fifteenth of ניסן, the day of יציאת מצרים
Righteous people
'The bag of silver,' read here as the צדיקים

phrases.english: "For fifteen":
this is the fifteenth of Nisan,
on which Israel was redeemed from Egypt.
"Silver": these are the righteous,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר ״צְרוֹר הַכֶּסֶף לָקַח בְּיָדוֹ״.
phrases.english: and so too it says: "He has taken the bag of silver with him."
phrases.notes: משלי 7:20

steps.triggerLanguage: ״בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר״ – זֶה חֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בְּנִיסָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same drasha, moving from the verb to the price
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Fifteen' hints to ט״ו בניסן; 'silver' means צדיקים.

steps.title: The barley measures stand for 45 righteous people
steps.stepSummary: The 'חומר' and 'לתך' of barley add up to 45, which stands for the 45 צדיקים in whose merit the world exists.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A חומר of barley and a לתך of barley': these are the forty-five צדיקים through whom the world exists.
steps.whatsHappening: The drasha moves to the end of the פסוק. The two barley measures are read as a hint to 45 צדיקים who keep the world going.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חומר is 30 סאה and a לתך is half of that, 15 סאה, so together they make 45. Because the number is split into 30 and 15, it also hints that the צדיקים are in two groups. That sets up the question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A large measure of 30 סאה
Half a חומר, 15 סאה
Exists through them, in their merit

phrases.english: "A chomer of barley and a half-chomer of barley":
phrases.notes: A חומר is 30 סאה and a לתך is 15, so together that's 45.

phrases.english: these are the forty-five righteous people
through whom the world continues to exist.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״חוֹמֶר שְׂעוֹרִים וְלֶתֶךְ שְׂעוֹרִים״ – אֵלּוּ אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשָּׁה צַדִּיקִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the drasha to the last words of the פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are 45 צדיקים in whose merit the world exists, hinted by the חומר and לתך of barley.

steps.title: Which group of righteous people is where
steps.stepSummary: The speaker says he does not know whether the 30 are in בבל and the 15 in ארץ ישראל, or the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: I do not know if thirty are here and fifteen in ארץ ישראל, or if thirty are in ארץ ישראל and fifteen here.
steps.whatsHappening: The 45 splits into 30 and 15, but the first פסוק does not say which group lives where. The גמרא raises this question to set up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The drasha has shown two groups but not where each one is. 'Here' means בבל, where the speaker is. Both options are still open until another פסוק settles it.

keyTerms.meaning: I do not know, a way of raising an open question
'Here,' meaning בבל

phrases.english: But I do not know if thirty are here
phrases.notes: 'Here' means בבל.

phrases.english: and fifteen are in Eretz Yisrael,

and fifteen are here.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ אִם שְׁלֹשִׁים כָּאן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a question that comes out of the 30/15 split in step 21
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Are the 30 צדיקים in ארץ ישראל or in בבל?

steps.title: A פסוק in זכריה shows the thirty are in ארץ ישראל
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in זכריה puts 'the thirty pieces of silver' in בית ה׳, so the 30 צדיקים are in ארץ ישראל and the 15 are in בבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says, 'And I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them into the treasury in the house of ה׳,' you must say: thirty are in ארץ ישראל and fifteen are here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from the last step with a פסוק in זכריה. Thirty 'silver' pieces go to the house of ה׳, so the group of thirty is in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silver was already shown to mean צדיקים (step 20). Here the number thirty is tied to the בית המקדש, which is in ארץ ישראל. So the leftover fifteen must be in בבל.

keyTerms.meaning: When the פסוק says, bringing a proof from another פסוק
You must therefore say, the conclusion
The house of ה׳, the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: 45 צדיקים keep the world going: 30 in ארץ ישראל and 15 in בבל. The numbers come from the barley measures in הושע and the thirty silver pieces in זכריה.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The thirty silver pieces go to בית ה׳, so the 30 צדיקים are in ארץ ישראל and the 15 in בבל.

steps.title: Most of the fifteen in בבל are in one בית כנסת
steps.stepSummary: אביי adds that most of the 15 צדיקים in בבל are found in a certain בית כנסת. He ties this to another פסוק in זכריה about 'thirty pieces of silver.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: most of them are found in the בית כנסת under the upper room. That is what the פסוק means: 'And I said to them: If it is good in your eyes, give me my wage, and if not, hold back. And they weighed out my wage, thirty pieces of silver.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a detail about the 15 צדיקים in בבל: most of them are found in one particular בית כנסת. He links this to a פסוק in זכריה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps said only that 15 צדיקים are in בבל. אביי narrows this down to a specific place. The גמרא brings the פסוק as a hint but does not spell out exactly how it connects.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Most of the 15 צדיקים in בבל are found in the בית כנסת דתותי אפתא, hinted in זכריה 11:12.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: the thirty are righteous people of the nations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה reads the 'thirty' as thirty righteous people among the nations of the world, in whose merit those nations survive.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: These thirty are thirty righteous people among the nations of the world. The nations of the world keep existing in their merit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new opinion about the 'thirty pieces of silver' from the פסוק in זכריה. רבי יהודה says the thirty are righteous non-Jews.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier steps said the thirty are צדיקים of ישראל living in ארץ ישראל. רבי יהודה moves the thirty to the nations of the world. The idea is the same: the world, or the nations, keep going in the merit of a small group of righteous people.

keyTerms.meaning: Righteous people among the non-Jewish nations
Keep existing because of them (in their merit)

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge to the earlier steps. It is simply a different way of reading the same number thirty.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
These are thirty righteous people of the nations of the world,
phrases.notes: 'These' means the 'thirty pieces of silver' in the פסוק, זכריה 11:12.

phrases.english: that the nations of the world exist in their merit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים צַדִּיקֵי אוּמּוֹת הָעוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different reading of the 'thirty pieces of silver' that steps 23-24 read as צדיקים of ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thirty are righteous people of the nations, in whose merit the nations exist.

steps.title: עולא: the thirty are מצוות the בני נח accepted
steps.stepSummary: עולא reads the 'thirty' as thirty מצוות the בני נח accepted, though they keep only three. He starts listing the three.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: These thirty are thirty מצוות that the בני נח accepted upon themselves, but they keep only three of them. One of them is...
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a third reading of the 'thirty': not people but מצוות the בני נח took on. The last word, 'one,' sets up the list of the three מצוות they still keep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the thirty are מצוות, not צדיקים. He adds a sharp point: the nations accepted thirty but keep only three. The list of the three begins with 'אחת' and continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: Descendants of Noach, meaning all non-Jewish humanity
Thirty מצוות
They keep only three

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the famous seven מצוות of בני נח. עולא is talking about thirty מצוות they accepted, of which they keep only three.

phrases.english: Ulla said:
These are thirty מצוות
that the descendants of Noach accepted upon themselves,
but they fulfill only three.
One [of them is]...
phrases.notes: The list of the three מצוות starts here and continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: עוּלָּא אָמַר: אֵלּוּ שְׁלֹשִׁים מִצְוֹת שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ עֲלֵיהֶם בְּנֵי נֹחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third reading of the same 'thirty,' alongside רבי יהודה's in step 25.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The thirty are מצוות the בני נח accepted, but they keep only three.
